newsitem.title: GREECE: Salomon cautious on Greek equities in short term.
newsitem.headline: Salomon cautious on Greek equities in short term.

text.p: Greek equities are overbought and expected to remain at current levels in the short term following this year's rally, said Salomon Brothers in its June global equity strategy report.

Along with Hungary, a cautious, neutral weighting was recommended for players with a three-month view. But the 12-month perspective is positive and Salomon expects the Athens bourse to outperform emerging market indices.

"The outstanding performance of the Greek and Hungarian markets this year makes us cautious. We believe that the markets are currently overbought but our 12-month view on both markets is positive," Salomon said.
It anticipated continuing positive results from sound macroeconomic policies.
"The long-awaited revaluation in the Greek market has occured, with the general share index rising by 75 percent this year," Salomon said.
"This expected revaluation was triggered by greater political stability, evident commitment to economic reform and EU convergence and a major liquidity drive as a result of declining T-bill yields."
The stock market rally was driven by bank shares on the back of lower interest rates and a restructuring of the banking sector.

"At this stage, with the bank index up by 88 percent in 1997, we expect the industrial sector to outperform. The traditional 30-50 percent valuation discount of the financial sector versus industrials has been reversed -- financials now trade at a 7.0 percent premium -- and at this stage a valuation adjustment is likely," Salomon said. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
